what: Angular signals are small reactive values: you read them like functions, derive new ones with computed, and Angular knows exactly which templates to refresh. Zoneless change detection then drops zone.js, so a screen updates only when a signal, an event listener or markForCheck says something changed.
like: Like sticky notes with strings attached: when one note changes, only the notes tied to it get re-read, instead of the teacher re-checking the whole wall after every sound in the room.
why: Less work per tap on a slow phone, because only affected views are checked
Smaller start-up cost: no zone.js patching of browser APIs
State flow is easy to trace: signal, computed, template

steps.d: signal(0) wraps a value; you read it by calling count() and change it with set or update.
computed() is lazy and memoized: it runs on first read and reuses its cached value until a dependency changes. Only signals actually read are tracked.
When a template reads a signal, Angular records that link. Updating the signal is one of the notifications that schedule change detection.
Without zone.js, change detection is triggered by signal updates, bound listeners, markForCheck (AsyncPipe calls it), setInput and dirty views being attached.
Use effect() only to talk to non-reactive APIs such as logging or a third-party widget. Prefer computed, linkedSignal or resource to derive state.

numbers.l: Angular version where zoneless is the default

compressed JS budget for a JS-heavy app to load in 3 s on a mid-range phone at P75

choices.d: Signals are for current state you read synchronously (a value now). RxJS is for events over time: debounce, cancel, retry, websockets. Bridge them with toSignal and toObservable.
If the result is data, use computed (or linkedSignal when it must also be writable). Effects are for side effects on non-reactive code, and are the last resort.
New apps on v21+ get zoneless by default. Older apps add provideZonelessChangeDetection (v20) and then remove zone.js from polyfills once every component notifies Angular properly.
OnPush is recommended with zoneless but not required; Default components still work if they receive one of the notifications.

instead.why: Same idea of fine-grained state, in the React world
For events over time such as typeahead, retries and cancellation

breaks.d: Code changes a plain field or a form value (for example setValue) with no signal, markForCheck or listener.
breaks.see: The screen does not update until something else happens
breaks.fix: Hold the state in a signal or call markForCheck; use the zoneless checker in dev

breaks.t: Signal read after await in an effect
breaks.d: Reads after an await are not tracked.
breaks.see: Effect runs once and never again
breaks.fix: Read signals before the await, or use untracked deliberately

breaks.d: onStable, onMicrotaskEmpty and isStable do nothing useful without zone.js.
breaks.see: Third-party code hangs waiting for stability
breaks.fix: Use afterNextRender or afterEveryRender, and PendingTasks for SSR

say: I hold current state in signals and derive with computed, and keep RxJS for event streams like typeahead and retries.
On low-end phones I go zoneless with OnPush-style components so a tap only checks the views whose signals changed, and I drop zone.js payload.
I keep effects rare: they are for side effects on non-reactive APIs, not for copying state around.

followups.q: Why not just use RxJS for everything?
followups.a: Observables need subscriptions and cleanup, and a template needs an initial value. Signals give synchronous reads and automatic dependency tracking; RxJS still wins for time-based work.

followups.q: What breaks when you remove zone.js?
followups.a: Anything that changed state without telling Angular: plain field mutations, unwrapped form updates and code waiting on NgZone stability events.

today: Zoneless is the default from Angular v21 and the provider has been stable since v20.2, so new Angular apps are signal-first and zone.js-free; the docs steer you to computed, linkedSignal and resource rather than effect.

check.q: In a zoneless app, which of these schedules change detection?
check.a: Updating a signal that a template reads
check.why: Without zone.js only explicit notifications such as signal updates, listeners and markForCheck schedule it.

check.a: A lazy, memoized, read-only derived signal
d: An effect that runs on every tick
check.why: It runs on first read and caches until a dependency changes.

check.q: When is effect() the right tool?
check.a: To call a non-reactive API such as logging or a third-party widget
d: To derive one signal from another
To fetch data on every render
check.why: The docs recommend computed, linkedSignal or resource for derivations and effect only for side effects.
